findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean squared distance and native endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.0 to 0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5]; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no observed affinity label is available to score coordinate contrasts against.

The curve-support audit selected 24 continuous contrast features under a rule requiring absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, exclusion of a scale floor and q < 0.05, with a fidelity rule of relative RMSE <= 0.35, quiet-node large-fit fraction <= 0.1 and zero strong sign-conflict nodes; this is a selection-enrichment criterion, not an absolute geometric descriptor.

The information audit reports 14 independent batches and explicitly states its comparison is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, that nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect, and that teacher score correlations are observational and not a validated affinity predictor.

Lineage support covers 14 complete-survival batches over 700 total batch nodes, but 349 nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, and multiple testing is BH jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests that are explicitly not terminal affinity effects; terminal metadata shows one future-resampling node per batch at terminal score time 0.99, outside the observed window.

hypotheses.direction: Increase weight on nodes whose validated absolute contrast change is favorable relative to comparison.
hypotheses.falsifier: No reproducible change in regional attention at observed score nodes, or a sign conflict exceeding the declared zero-strong-sign-conflict fidelity rule.
hypotheses.observable: Registered temporal_region attention weight at observed score nodes versus the static regional weight.
hypotheses.scope: Observed score-time window [0.0,0.49] only; no extrapolation beyond the observed support.
hypotheses.statement: Signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts at observed selection nodes over the complete observed window can be expressed as a time-conditioned regional attention change using the registered temporal_region recipe, which alters regional attention at observed score nodes using the same static teachers and validated absolute contrast changes.

hypotheses.direction: Down-weight coordinate hypotheses whose selection direction is contradicted by survival credit.
hypotheses.falsifier: Selection and survival directions agree in sign across batches within the declared batch-direction fraction threshold.
hypotheses.observable: Sign agreement between selection-node contrast direction and survival-credit direction per independent batch.
hypotheses.scope: 14 independent batches; survival tests are not terminal affinity effects.
hypotheses.statement: Immediate selection evidence and later survival or quality credit may disagree in direction, and any such disagreement should reorder coordinate priorities rather than be averaged into a single point estimate.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit and the immediate-versus-descendant comparison is unavailable.
The information audit states its metrics are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, so no claim about the executed reward's affinity effect can be made from it.

Ancestral coverage is sparse (349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors, 531 with fewer than 6), so descendant survival credit is subject to survivor bias and cannot be treated as an unbiased later-label estimate.

No uncertainty- or multiplicity-adjusted ranking of coordinate hypotheses beyond the delivered selection rule and BH-adjusted survival tests was computed here; a concrete priority decision differing from point-estimate ranking is therefore not demonstrated.

Continuous contrast curves were not read at node level in this response, so sign changes, fit fidelity and rate changes across the full observed support remain unverified beyond the aggregate curve-support audit.
No parent-child increment contrast or turnover residual comparison was performed, so within-path change versus changing cohort composition is not resolved.
No current study outcome data are available to this role, so no coordinate intervention can be validated as improving final predicted affinity.
